text.p: Bangladesh, where half the population lives below the poverty line, is home to more than 2,500 dollar multi-millionaires, a central bank official said on Friday.
They owned a total of about 850 billion taka ($19.3 billion) in bank deposits and much more in other assets, said the official, who declined to be named.
"It's not true that we are all poor. A segment of our population is very rich, some owning more than one billion taka ($22.6 million) each," he said.
He said there were only about 10 Bangladeshis owning more than 10 million taka in the 1970s, around 100 in the 1980s and at least 500 now.
"The rising number of multi-millionaires, however, indicates that wealth is accumulated in a few hands, leaving the vast majority in poverty," he told Reuters.
